newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kinkel wants Britain "at the heart of Europe".
newsitem.headline: Kinkel wants Britain "at the heart of Europe".

text.p: Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said on Thursday in a review of Bonn's European policy that Germany wanted Britain to be "at the heart of Europe" and not off on its fringes.

Addressing parliament in Bonn, Kinkel said Germany and France were working together to propose new steps towards further integration of the European Union before the group's next summit in December in Dublin.

"We also want to see Britain 'at the heart of Europe' and not on its periphery," he said, repeating the pro-European phrase Prime Minister John Major used on his first visit to Germany as British leader in March 1991.
Kinkel added: "But for that, a few things have to be moved forward."
Major has come under attack by Euro-sceptics at this week's Conservative Party conference in Bournemouth for taking a wait-and-see attitude towards the EU's planned single currency.
On Wednesday, he told delegates it was essential to maintain Britain's influence in negotiations on how the new money would work even if Britain did not eventually join.
Kinkel did not spell out where he felt Britain had to modify its policies to come more in line with its EU partners.
But his list of priorities for the inter-governmental conference deliberating a reform of the Maastricht treaty included several points London opposes.

He called for a single European currency in 1999, more majority voting in the EU, a strengthening of the European Parliament and the transformation of the Western European Union into the EU's defence arm.
